sources.entry: The USE Method - Sets the checklist that finds the saturated resource before any profiler is opened.

summary.title: The USE Method
summary.one_liner: The USE Method teaches you to check utilization, saturation, and errors for every system resource to quickly find bottlenecks before reaching for profilers.
keywords: how to find server bottleneck quickly
takeaways: For every resource, check utilization, saturation, and errors; this is meant to be done early to find systemic bottlenecks.
Utilization is usually expressed as a percent over an interval, saturation as queue length, and errors as counts.
Long-interval averages can hide short bursts of 100% utilization, so saturation and short-interval metrics matter.
Build a resource list (CPUs, memory, network, storage, controllers, interconnects) and fill in OS-specific metrics to make a checklist.
The method finds bottlenecks and errors but not every issue; it is one tool alongside latency-based methods like Method R.
summary.summary: Brendan Gregg presents the USE Method, a methodology that starts by asking questions about each system resource (CPUs, memory, network interfaces, storage, controllers, interconnects) and checking utilization, saturation, and errors. The page explains terminology, gives example metric tables, and suggests interpretation rules such as treating sustained utilization above about 70% as a potential problem. It contrasts the approach with a tools-based checklist and with latency-based methods, and applies the same thinking to cloud resource controls and, as an example, the Apollo Lunar Module guidance computer. OS-specific checklists are linked from the page, which also lists related publications and talks.
